findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled and the cursor offset is negative, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError/AssertionError. A client-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` therefore causes a 500 error rather than the advertised 'reverse pagination'. The negative-offset branch should be removed and the offset validated as non-negative.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a user-controlled negative offset on a prev cursor (e.g. `123:-10:1`) reach `queryset[offset:stop]`. Django querysets reject negative slicing, so every BasePaginator endpoint in Sentry can be made to return a 500 with a crafted cursor. Clamp the offset with `max(0, offset)` in all cases, or reject negative offsets in Cursor parsing.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the attribute, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number. The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by='-datetime'`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError on any non-empty page. Cursor values are also compared against the datetime column as plain integers. The optimized path is broken whenever there are results; it should reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor-value conversion.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated even for superusers who are not members, and `or` only short-circuits when `is_superuser` is true. Any other request whose context has no member, such as API tokens or staff, raises AttributeError. Use a None-safe check on `member` before reading `has_global_access`.

findings.title: Comments claim unsafe behavior is safe
findings.body: The comments at lines 878-879 say negative offsets 'enable access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' and are 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'. No validation bounds the cursor offset at all. The feature is driven entirely by a client-controlled query param and cursor, so these comments misrepresent the risk. There are also no tests for the new paginator or the endpoint branch.
